title: Vibrant Katsuramuki Brazilian Beets Bowl
description: A bitter, gooey, indulgent Brazilian dish featuring beets, katsuramuki-cut, perfect for a Mediterranean-inspired meal. This recipe serves as a unique twist on traditional Brazilian cuisine.

ingredients.name: Beets
ingredients.notes: any color, but red beets work best for color

instructions: Chop 2 medium beets into thin strips, using a mandoline for optimal katsuramuki-cut texture.
Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat.
Add 1 small onion, diced, and saut86t until translucent, 3-4 minutes.
Add 2 cloves of minced garlic and cook for an additional 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add 2 cups of water and 1 tablespoon of soy sauce to the saucepan.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the beets are tender.
Using a slotted spoon, transfer the beets to a blender and puree until smooth.
Strain the cooking liquid into a small bowl, discarding the solids.
In a large saucepan, combine 2 tablespoons of olive oil, 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, and 2 tablespoons of honey.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 5-7 minutes, until thickened slightly.
Stir in 1 tablespoon of lemon juice and 1 teaspoon of grated ginger.
To assemble the bowls, place 1/4 cup of cooked quinoa in the bottom of a mason jar.
Add 1/2 cup of the beet puree on top of the quinoa, followed by 1/2 cup of the warm sauce and 1/4 cup of toasted almonds.
Garnish with fresh cilantro, if desired
